international.title: Australian politics live: Penny Wong to defend US alliance; Coalition condemns Vanuatu deal
international.summary: Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast The Coalition has come out against a security agreement with Vanuatu because of objections to “binding conditions relating to the achievement of renewable energy and climate targets”. In June, prime minister, Anthony Albanese , and his Vanuatu counterpart, Jotham Napat , signed the Nakamal agreement in Canberra that rules out the use of its territory for foreign military bases. We acknowledge the legitimate concerns Vanuatu and other Pacific Island nations have regarding climate change and its impacts on their communities, economies, and national security. However, Coalition members object to clauses … that limit the ability of future governments to change current climate and energy policy settings, by creating binding conditions relating to the achievement of renewable energy and climate targets. Such a policy would do is surrender a central source of Australian strategic weight at precisely the moment we need every opportunity for influence available to us. What they would do is give us fewer choices and leave us more vulnerable, reducing our capacity to contribute to a regional balance in which our sovereignty can be protected. Continue reading...
